key_insight: Combining bidirectional decoding with evolutionary operators lets a language model explore and iteratively improve candidate outputs beyond high-probability autoregressive paths, yielding higher-quality solutions guided by denser verification signals.
problem_solved: Overcomes two core limitations of common search strategies (best-of-N, tree search): reliance on sparse/weak verification signals and restricted exploration confined to high-probability autoregressive generations.
method: Maintain a population of candidate outputs and generate proposals using bidirectional decoding (both forward and backward completion) to access low-probability but potentially better regions of the output space.
Apply evolutionary operators—mutation, crossover, and selection—combined with richer fitness evaluations (e.g., learned verifiers or multi-criterion checks) to rank and refine candidates.
Iteratively evolve the population (selection → variation → evaluation) to produce higher-quality outputs for inference and to generate improved training samples for self-improvement.
impact: Enables more robust, sample-efficient self-improvement of language models and agentic systems by expanding exploration and providing stronger internal feedback—leading to higher-quality outputs with less human labeling and fewer search samples.

paper_title: Self-Improving Language Models with Bidirectional Evolutionary Search
paper_authors: Guowei Xu, Zhenting Qi, Huangyuan Su, Weirui Ye, Himabindu Lakkaraju
